thread:
jose: Hi all, first day! Unboxed my MB Air M3 and tried to install Homebrew/Docker but installs fail with 'permission denied' and System Settings shows 'Local admin disabled by policy'. I need to get a dev environment up — any JIT admin flow?

it-support: welcome jose! we lock local admin by default. we do have a Just-In-Time temporary admin flow. can you share your serial (DM if preferred)? also which installer errors are you seeing?

jose: serial C02AB2ZZZZZZ. errors when running brew install --cask docker: 

```
Error: Permission denied @ rb_sysopen - /usr/local/bin/brew
```

also installer popups ask to allow kernel extensions but buttons are greyed out.

mdm-bot: Policy note for C02AB2ZZZZZZ: allow_local_admin = false, runtime_policy = standard, pending_jit_request = none.

it-support: thanks. we'll spin up a JIT admin window for you for 3 hours. creating request now.

it-support: @jose granted temporary admin: username temp-jose-exp1957010130, expires 1957010130. DMing password and one-time sudo token. you'll see an Okta approval prompt — accept to activate.

okta-bot: Action required: Approve temporary admin access for jose (expire in 3h). Approve link sent to jose's phone.

jose: approved on phone. I see the account in Users & Groups and can sudo. thanks.

devex: heads up — for Docker on macOS Ventura/Monterey/Sequoia we prefer the Apple-silicon brew package path. run these commands as sudo once: 

```
/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"
sudo /opt/homebrew/bin/brew install --cask docker
```

and then restart and open Docker app once so it registers the helper.

jose: did that. Docker installed and launched. the kernel extension prompt still required me to go to System Settings > Privacy & Security > Allow and click 'Allow' after unlocking. it worked.

it-support: one more thing: FileVault prompts during setup? we require disk encryption.

jose: yeah FileVault prompt appeared during first login; I enabled it. do you need the recovery key?

okta-bot: Okta device escrow: recovery key recorded for C02AB2ZZZZZZ by jose at 1957010005.

it-support: good. we'll mark the JIT admin session as active and it will auto-revoke at expiry. post-expiry, if you need more admin time open a new request with justification (e.g., native deps build).

devex: note for future hires: if you need persistent dev privileges we recommend using devcontainers or a dedicated dev VM to avoid changing company policy.

jose: amazing — thanks everyone. first-week checklist item: complete. :)

it-support: Closing notes: root cause = org policy disables local admin; mitigation = Okta/JIT temporary admin with audit trail. closing thread unless you hit more blockers. :thumbsup:
